newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee jumps sharply as upswing resumes.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee jumps sharply as upswing resumes.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices bounced back from early losses to close sharply higher on Monday, bolstered by a late-session round of speculative buying, dealers said.
After posting losses the past two consecutive sessions, market participants said downward momentum dried up.
"It corrected the last two days and it corrected this morning," said one dealer. "It just felt like it was over."

The afternoon run up was led by the most-active May contract, which surged 9.50 cents per lb on the day to 199.30 cents, after peaking at 200.00 cents. Earlier in the session, speculative profit-taking and producer sales knocked May to a low of 185.20 cents.
Roaster interest toward the lows helped stem losses and prevented a test of key support at 185.00-184.00 cents per lb basis May.
Traders also said the market may have been given a boost by rumors that leading roaster Folgers would raise its retail price on a 13-ounce can of ground coffee by 15 cents effective immediately.

After the close of business, Folgers released a statement confirming that it will raise the list price on its standard 13-ounce can by 15 cents immediately due to higher prices of green coffee on the world's futures markets.
The increase, which brings the new price for a standard can to $2.86, comes only one week after a 45-cent increase in the price of Folgers 13-ounce can of ground coffee took effect.
Analysts and traders said the market's resumption of its recent bull run, in which prices have risen by more than 50 percent, continued to be fueled by supply concerns.

"Basically, it keeps rising on the reality of short supply," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "And apprehensiveness of 'Can I get the coffee I need?' No one has experienced any relief on the prospect of tight stocks"
Prendergast said the market appeared poised to continue to trend higher at least until the March contract goes off the board next Tuesday.
"Momentum is clearly on the upside," she said. "It has declared itself now and it looks like it will go up to 230 cents."
After Monday's close, the head of the primary commodities department at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry said the country's 1997/98 coffee crop could be up to 22 million 60-kg bags.
"It's between 20 and 22 million bags," Mauricio Assis told reporters after a meeting with soluble coffee industry representatives.
Previously, the Brazilian government said it was working with a range between 18 million and 20 million bags for the coming harvest.

In other news, certified coffee stocks grew for the third day in a row, reaching 30,844 60-kg bags as of March 7, the CSCE reported after the close of trading. There were an additional 23,289 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
Friday's turnover was estimated at 9,720 lots, compared with Friday's official tally of 14,222 lots.
